plate_findings.evidence: Eruptive and tuberoeruptive xanthomas. + Eruptive xanthomas in the forearms, legs, back

findings.label: Tuberous xanthoma of elbows and knees

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Top-left panel shows leg with multiple yellowish papules consistent with captioned eruptive xanthomas in legs in severe hypertriglyceridemia case routed to familial dysbetalipoproteinemia. B: Top-right panel shows arm/elbow with eruptive papules and larger tuberoeruptive lesions, matching caption and in-text tuberoeruptive xanthomas on elbows. C: Bottom-left panel shows shoulder/upper arm with multiple eruptive papular xanthomas as captioned. D: Bottom-right panel shows back with numerous eruptive papules consistent with captioned eruptive xanthomas in back.
panels.attribution_text: Zahedi et al. Case Report: Management of a Patient With Chylomicronemia Syndrome During Pregnancy With Medical Nutrition Therapy.. Frontiers in nutrition 2021. doi:10.3389/fnut.2021.602938. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: ear-old in the first pregnancy (G1P0Ab0), with a severe HTG presented in the second trimester of pregnancy. Eruptive xanthomas in the forearms, legs, back, and tuberoeruptive xanthomas on her elbows (Figure 1) occurred in the 27th week of pregnancy, and she was admitted to a hospital in November 2019. Her serum lipoprotein profile was as follows: fasting TG: 6,620 mg/dL, total cholesterol: 459 mg/dL, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C): 76 mg/dL, and serum amylase and lipase levels were within normal limits.
